text:
alex: Heads-up: customers report that traffic stays on hosted nodes even after dedicated pools come online. This is causing cost and SLA blips during canaries.

maya: Is this the 24h routing affinity behavior? I thought we lowered it.

devon: It's still 24h in the runtime handshake. Probe returns capability JSON and we set a routing cookie / affinity key on first connect.

gina: 24h feels excessive for rollouts. Why was it that long originally?

alex: Avoided mid-session backend switches for long-lived flows. But most of our flows are short-lived; 24h is overkill and blocks fast cutovers.

samir: We should decide between two patterns:
- control-driven manifests (control plane tells clients where to route)
- runtime-advertised capabilities (runtime tells clients, client decides)
Both have tradeoffs around partition tolerance, privacy, and churn.

maya: For Private, manifest push is fine because the control plane link is internal. But hosted needs runtime autonomy when control plane latency spikes.

devon: Security: manifest push exposes model lists and capacity if not designed carefully. Private requires no model names leave the customer site without explicit consent.

gina: Proposal: hybrid "versioned capability" model. Runtime only reveals an opaque capability_version hash + tiny boolean attrs. Control plane maps that version to routing decisions.

samir: Implementation sketch:
1) Runtime probe -> returns capability_version (sha256) + flags: {streams: true/false, seq_len_hint: short/long}
2) Clients publish capability_version to control plane (or subscribe)
3) Control plane evaluates policy + publishes route_affinity for that capability_version
4) Clients cache route_affinity with a short TTL (e.g., 5m) and obey until refreshed

maya: TTL ~5m seems like a sweet spot but increases control plane update rate. We'll need delta batching and a push/delta API (SSE or WebSocket) to avoid polling.

devon: Clients should also have deterministic local fallback if control plane is unreachable: a simple ranking of compatible backends based on capability_version (no secrets leaked).

gina: Also need to avoid eviction storms when an affinity flips: recommend a randomized jitter window for rebind attempts and staggered backoff per client instance.

alex: Test matrix (to include in RFC):
- T1: Hosted -> Dedicated rollout with control plane available
- T2: Dedicated healthy but control plane partitioned (simulate SSE outage)
- T3: Private on-prem where capability metadata must remain opaque
- T4: High-client-count churn test to measure control plane delta QPS

samir: I'll prototype a delta emitter and publish a rate model. We should define quotas: max delta events/sec per region and group.

maya: I'll own security constraints: what attributes are allowed in runtime probe for Private installs, and the KMS consent flow if control plane needs to ingest identity tokens.

devon: I'll add the client TTL heuristics, jitter/backoff, and implement capability_version compute in the runtime shim. Also wire up metrics: affinity_rebind_attempts, affinity_success_rate.

gina: I'll build the load test harness to simulate millions of short connects and measure eviction events and delta fanout.

alex: Owners agreed. I'll draft the RFC that includes feature matrix, sequence diagrams, metrics, and rollout plan. Want rough perf targets: control plane delta < 5000/sec at GA with batching.

deploy-bot: Reminder: created infra issue infra/hosting-affinity-428 (AUTO)

maya: Metrics to include in RFC: affinity_cache_ttl, delta_emit_rate, delta_subscriber_errors, rebind_jitter_ms_p95, private_probe_attr_leaks

samir: One more: define a small control-plane API contract:
- POST /register_capability {capability_version, runtime_id}
- GET /affinity_delta?since=cursor -> SSE stream of {capability_version, route_affinity, cursor}
Keep payloads minimal (no model names for private runtimes).

devon: For safety, clients should treat route_affinity as advisory. If a runtime reports inability to comply (capacity), it can return a short negative ack and control plane will back off.

gina: I'll add fuzz tests that flip affinity mappings quickly to ensure jitter/backoff prevents waves.

alex: Timeline: RFC draft by EOD Tue, arch sync Thu for review. Great.
